findings.title: Commits and PR body carry Claude/Anthropic attribution trailers, violating instructions
findings.claim: Commits f545c28a, 5e25ebdb, 69da8f5b each carry a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer (one has two), and the PR body ends with a 'Generated with Claude Code' line, violating the global instruction forbidding this attribution; messages and PR body should be rewritten before merging.

findings.title: test_data_sink_impl is abstract because it only overrides put(std::span<...>)
findings.claim: Below SEASTAR_API_LEVEL 9, put(net::packet) is pure virtual, so test_data_sink_impl remains abstract and std::make_unique fails to compile; it should guard both put() variants like loopback_socket.hh does.

findings.title: Non-closed_error exception from hook can cause use-after-free during test teardown
findings.claim: If the hook throws anything other than rpc::closed_error, the thread unwinds with write_buf.close() still parked on release_close, and sink/source are destroyed dropping the last connection refs while stream_close() and _stopped are still pending, which could surface as a use-after-free rather than a clean failure; suggests capturing outcome with then_wrapped into an exception_ptr, releasing, joining, then asserting.

findings.title: Stream handler test is not shard-safe under --smp 2
findings.claim: Under --smp 2 the loopback connect round-robins server shards, so the stream handler can run on shard 1 while writing server_done and pushing into server_factory.hooks, both shard-0 objects; noted as the same pattern as existing stream_test_func so not new, but still not shard-safe.

findings.title: const_cast used to push into hooks instead of declaring the member mutable
findings.claim: The code does const_cast<hook_capturing_compressor_factory*>(this)->hooks.push_back(...); hooks should be declared mutable instead.

findings.title: Comment misstates where the test fails without the fix
findings.claim: The closing comment says destruction is where ~output_stream() asserts, but after the ten yield()s the flush poller has normally already run, so without the fix the test actually fails on put_after_close at line 2032, not on the assert; the commit message states this correctly and the comment should be aligned with it.

findings.title: then_wrapped lambda parameter f shadows the enclosing auto f
findings.claim: The then_wrapped lambda parameter named f shadows the enclosing auto f variable and should be renamed.

findings.title: _stream_closing field is placed away from the related _sink_closed/_source_closed fields
findings.claim: _stream_closing would read better placed next to _sink_closed/_source_closed at lines 301-302, which it pairs with.

findings.title: Parent client's compressor hook behavior during client::stop() left unexamined
findings.claim: The parent client's compressor hook during client::stop() was set aside as out of scope, noted as already refused via _error.

findings.title: Unclear whether external compressors handle closed_error from send_empty_frame
findings.claim: Whether external compressors cope with closed_error thrown from send_empty_frame was set aside as out of scope and not investigated.

findings.title: Pre-existing abort()/stream_close()/shutdown_output() ordering race not investigated
findings.claim: A pre-existing abort()-races-stream_close() shutdown_output() ordering issue was set aside as out of scope and not investigated.

findings.title: Documentation does not mention the new failure mode
findings.claim: doc/rpc-compression.md does not mention the new failure mode introduced by this change; set aside as out of scope.

findings.title: Layout change to rpc::connection in a public header
findings.claim: The layout change to rpc::connection in a public header was set aside as out of scope since Seastar makes no ABI promise.
